brewing.notes: A safe starting point for green tea: cooler water, short steeps, then adjust by taste.

description:
A Libyan way of serving tea with peanuts; the name marks a preparation rather than a growing region.

This is a way of preparing tea more than a tea you buy under one name, so the recipe and the base tea change from one maker to the next.

images.author: Abdulgahniessadi
images.alt: Small glasses of dark red Libyan tea filled with peanuts on a tray

processing: Made from a green base tea according to the recipe; the method varies.
harvest_season: Not tied to a harvest: it depends on the base tea.
appearance_dry: Green leaf whose shape depends on the maker, as is usual for regional green teas.
appearance_wet: Usually soft green leaf that opens up in the water.
taste_profile: Expect what green teas usually give: fresh, vegetal and lightly sweet.
vintage_note: Not sold by vintage: it is made from whatever base tea the maker keeps, so freshness of the base matters more than the year.
